header.name: IT AND SOCIETY
header.description: The Course will give a brief historical and sociological context to the emergence of Information technology and its spread from the specialist field of military intelligence to the everyday world of civilian use. It will analyse the effect of this new technology on industrial work culture, finance and education leading to new spatial, regional and global ways of doing business, creating knowledge and demarcating sovereignty. It will take up Silicon Valley and Bangalore briefly as case studies explaining this phenomena. It will next focus on the internet and its impact on new forms of human communication, warfare, business, governance, education and medicine. On the cultural front it will examine the interplay bewteen family and sociality, gender and age, transnationality and work, entrepreneurship and labour under conditions of the Knowledge Society or the New Economy. The convergence of mobile with internet technologies will be examined for the development of political movements and political cultures in democratic governance with the attendant concerns of privacy, surveillance, cyber security and violence . In India, the public culture of ICT4D will be compared with the start-up culture of doing business and new forms of e-governance today. The problem of the Digital Divide will be highlighted against the backdrop of new youth aspirations, middle class wealth creation and rural urban distinctions. New forms of aggressive identity- seeking globally, through new forms of IT-based entertainment, networked community formation and religious proselytisation, leading to terror, violence and risk will be outlined, especially for the everyday world of the young. Finally, the need for appropriate laws and ethical constraints to address these social concerns will be examined at the personal and professional level.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Critically examine IT in its social and historical context

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Compare and analyse interaction of IT and society, its nature and scope, relative to conventional technologies

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Conceptually link global economic, political and cultural change with close personal experience of IT in work, life and play.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text:
1) Assess new codes for ethics and social responsibility given IT’s power and pervasiveness.
2) Research and evaluate existing case studies of IT based business and governance solutions to human problems in India
